title: Electronic Missile Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-948D. Military Occupational Specialty 948D—Electronic Missile Systems Maintenance
Warrant Officer
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites.AR 135-100, DA PAM 601-6, and DA PAM 611-21.
   c. MOS 948D. MOS 948D is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are: 94A, 94M,
94P, 94S, 94T, 94W and 94Z.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0—No special qualifications.
        (2) 8—Instructor.
        (3) P—Parachutist.
        (4) T—Transition
        (5) Z-Research, Development, Test and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI.
        (1) Refer to DA PAM 611-21 table 6-6 (listing of universal ASIs associated with all Warrant
Officer MOSs)
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must -
              (a) Successfully complete the Electronic Missile Systems Maintenance Warrant
Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
              (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use
of upper and lower extremities per AR 40-501.

        (2) CW3 must -
              (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f(1) above.
              (b) Successfully complete the Electronic Missile Maintenance Warrant Officer
Advanced Course (WOAC).
        (3) CW4 must
              (a) Meet qualifications as listed for in paragraph f(2) above.
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must see MOS 948E.
    g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2-
              (a) Implements proper crime prevention, security and safety (IAW OSHA)
procedures.
              (b) Employs digital switching theory, logic, computer fundamentals and infrared
fundamentals applicable to the Army’s missile systems and associated equipment. Responsible
for the operation of maintenance support teams and field level maintenance facilities. Monitor unit
status reporting requirements for tactical missile units and associated support elements.
Supervise field level maintenance repair, organic tools, test sets, and associated training
equipment. Estimates supply requirements, observes work practices, and detects and corrects
improper procedures and techniques. Initiates and monitors Product Quality descripency report
(PDQR) Supply Discrepancy Report (SDR) engineering changes proposal (ECP) documents.
Ensures quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) procedures are followed, to include
calibration.
              (c) Applies theory and fundamentals of solid-state devices and optics employed in
guidance and sighting systems. Directs test procedures, diagnostic system analysis and
troubleshooting techniques. Directs and assists personnel in solving complex problems of
diagnosis, and modification, of automated test equipment used in support of missile systems.
              (d) Directs the operation of Logistics Information Systems (LIS) for field level repairs
and parts. Develops, coordinates, updates, and applies internal administration procedures to
requisition, receive, issue, and store repair parts, tools, publication, supplies, appropriates shop
supply procedures and maintenance related items.
              (e) Advises commanders on technical aspects of missile systems maintenance,
support testing and supply.
                (f) Instructs subordinates in operating procedures, maintenance techniques,
interpreting technical data used in care of special tools and supporting equipment, as well as The
Army Maintenance Management System (TAMMS).
               (g) Establishes, monitors, and maintains a comprehensive environmental protection
program in accordance with international, national and local directives.
          (2) CW3 -
               (a) Performs duties described in para g(1) above.
               (b) Provides technical guidance and direction to subordinate elements and serves as
a technical or tactical advisor for missile systems. Manages the Army repair parts system and
performs as a liaison to supported units to determine future support requirements and satisfaction
with current support requirements.
               (c) Develops and writes training material, and instructs/supervises at Army service
schools. Serve as a service school instructor or project officer at staff level.
               (d) Performs duties as a research, development, test, and evaluation technician.
               (e) Is proficient in all aspects of missile maintenance operations and manages/directs
maintenance operations in a tactical environment.
               (f) Analyzes complex malfunctions occurring in missile systems and auxiliary
equipment.
               (g) Directs operations, maintenance, and calibrations of the ATE.
               (h) Develops, implements, and monitors programs of instruction that enhance training
of other warrant officer and enlisted MOSs.
               (i) Monitors, identifies, and rectifies anomalies in the requisition life cycle of repair
parts requisitions.
               (j) Assists the commander or maintenance control officer in the application of
available automation resources to optimize shop operations.
         (3) CW4-
               (a) Is proficient in the duties described for the CW3 listed in paragraph g(2).
               (b) Performs duties and serves with procurement as a research, development, test,
and evaluation technician.
               (c) Presents written or oral briefings to line, staff, and professional personnel on
maintenance and related subject matters and provide staff studies or papers on pertinent
maintenance and personnel issues.
               (d) Provides technical and tactical assistance at any echelon of command or support
activity for the U.S. Army or liaison activities with allied armies.
               (e) Monitors, coordinate, analyze contracting, procurement, and material acquisition
programs for new and existing electronic equipment. Provides data and technical guidance
concerning future requirements, modification work order (MWO), product improvement program
(PIP), and related program information that has an impact upon Life Cycle Systems Management
(LCSM) of electronic missile equipment.
               (f) Provides coordination between military and industry during development, testing,
and fielding of new electronic missile equipment.
               (g) Manages the development of training packages to ensure Army personnel are
prepared to operate and maintain the new systems prior to fielding.
         (4) CW5 must see MOS 948E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 36 shuttles) is
required in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals W01/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
               (a) Table 8-948D-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
               (b) Table 8-948D-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
